combinations.name: construction + raid interruption
combinations.coupling: Both a settlement's active construction commission and a raid's contact/compensation draw an exact water reservation from the SAME survey via KingdomWaterDebit.ReserveExactStore/ReserveExactWater: construction at Growth/KingdomCommission.cs:205 (ReserveExactWater) and Growth/KingdomConstruction.Funding.cs:68, raid contact at Raids/KingdomRaids.06.AttackResolutionAndOutbox.cs:107-108 (ReserveExactStore). KingdomWaterDebit.cs:156 is the shared reservation authority both lanes call into.
combinations.prerequisites: a founded settlement with an in-progress construction commission (Working phase, unfinished) AND a raid contact/attack resolved against the same zone within the same interval
combinations.invariants: conservation of water: sum of all outstanding reservations against the survey never exceeds the real store census; a raid's compensation debit and a construction job's funding debit against the same store never double-reserve the same drams; custody by reference (the construction job's own Water reservation object is never silently reused or mutated by the raid's debit path)
combinations.seed_turn_matrix: one fixed seed; 2 turn-order variants (raid resolves before vs after the construction job's daily funding poll in the same tick window); no further seed variation -- this is a two-cell matrix, not a sweep
combinations.expected_failure_rows: a torn/negative water census after both debits settle; a construction job stuck Funded with a Water reservation object no longer in Reserved state but no journaled cause
combinations.reusable_seams: Harness/KingdomTeardownNativeProvider.cs (commission half) + Harness/KingdomRaidContactNativeProvider.cs (contact half) -- no existing seam runs both together

combinations.name: multiple cities + travel + save/load
combinations.coupling: CORRECTED: production has ONE realm KingdomSystem, not one System per city. A second 'city' is a second, non-seat KingdomSettlement row in System.SettlementTopology (Core/KingdomSystem.z08.SettlementTopology.cs:22, NonSeatSettlements()), each carrying its own KingdomCityBook with its own SettlementId (Core/KingdomSystem.z25.IdentityNormalization.cs:167-178, City.SettlementId assigned per-row), and its own claimed zone (Core/KingdomSystem.z08.Settlements.cs:61, TrySeat/FindNonSeatSettlementByZone). Travel's loaded-index scan is per-zone (Harness/KingdomCity.NativeTravelDemand.cs:38). The shared authority is this single System's settlement-topology registry each non-seat row claims a slot in -- no driver currently founds a second settlement row at all (row 12, NONE), so this coupling is untested even at the single-behaviour level.
combinations.prerequisites: two founded settlements in the same save AND at least one travel (away/return) cycle for a resident of one of them, followed by a save/cold-load
combinations.invariants: settlement isolation WITHIN the one System: two non-seat KingdomSettlement rows carry distinct SettlementId/City books and distinct claimed zones; a travel scan against settlement A's zone never reads or credits settlement B's stockpile/roster; save/cold-load reproduces every settlement row's SettlementId/City/ClaimedZones distinctly (no merged or aliased KingdomSettlement row after reload)
combinations.seed_turn_matrix: one fixed seed; single scenario shape (found city A, found city B, travel one resident of A away and back, save, cold-load, re-assert both cities' rosters/stock unchanged) -- not a sweep, a single bounded chain
